newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs called steady-firm - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs called steady-firm - trade.

text.p: Cash hog prices were called steady to possibly $0.50 per cwt higher Friday at Midwest direct markets, cash dealers said.

Iowa and Illinois dealers said most packers in those areas appear to have Friday's slaughter needs covered and will be buying for Monday. Indiana sources said a few plants in that area will need hogs for Saturday slaughter.
Competition for hogs may ease slightly because two Hormel Foods Corp plants will be closed Monday, dealers said.
A Hormel spokeswoman said its Fremont, Neb., hog slaughtering plant and its Austin, Minn., pork processing plant will be closed Monday for the Veteran's Day holiday.
Also, Quality Pork Processing Inc's hog slaughtering plant in Austin will be closed Monday. The plant provides fresh pork to Hormel's Austin pork plant.
Spokespersons for other meat packers were unavailable for comment regarding Monday's operations.
